text.en: Your school bag holds a set of books. Mathematics uses the word set for any well-defined collection of objects, and it is the language in which later ideas are written.

A set is a well-defined collection of distinct objects, called its elements; we write x belongs to A as x in A.
Roster form lists the elements: A = {1, 2, 3, 4}. Set-builder form gives a rule: A = {x : x is a natural number less than 5}.
The number of elements of a finite set A is its cardinal number, n(A).
The empty set has no elements and is written as { } or the symbol phi.
A set is a subset of B if every element of A is in B, written A is contained in B. The empty set is a subset of every set.
Two sets are equal if they have exactly the same elements; equivalent sets have the same number of elements.
The power set of A is the set of all subsets of A; if n(A) = m it has 2^m elements.

problem.en: List all subsets of A = {a, b} and give the number of elements of its power set.

text.en: Subsets with no element: { }. With one element: {a}, {b}. With two: {a, b}.
